input: Get a mold inspection done in the basement

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is a visual-only inspection or a full air/surface sampling inspection changes who to hire, how long it takes, and what the deliverable looks like.
Whether this is a primary residence, rental property, or a home being bought/sold changes urgency, who is responsible, and what remediation steps may follow.
Knowing if they already have a specific inspector in mind or need help finding one determines the first action — research vs. scheduling.
A hard deadline (e.g., closing date, lease renewal, health concern) changes how quickly the task must be completed and whether expedited services are needed.
Inspections range from ~$200 for visual-only to $1,000+ for full lab testing; budget shapes which option is viable.
The end goal — a clean bill of health, a written report for a landlord/buyer, or guidance on remediation — defines what a successful inspection outcome looks like.
Knowing whether there is already a suspected problem area, visible mold, or a musty smell helps the inspector prepare and affects what parts of the basement need attention.

gold.taskTitle: Get a mold inspection done in the basement
gold.taskDescription: Arrange and complete a mold inspection in the basement of a property.

questions.title: What type of inspection do you need — visual only or lab testing?
questions.description: Determine whether the user needs a basic visual walkthrough or a full inspection with air/surface samples sent to a lab.

questions.title: Is this a home you own, rent, or are buying or selling?
questions.description: Clarify the property relationship to understand who is responsible and what the inspection will be used for.

questions.title: Do you already have an inspector in mind, or need to find one?
questions.description: Establish whether the next step is researching and vetting inspectors or simply scheduling an existing contact.

questions.title: Is there a deadline this inspection needs to be completed by?
questions.description: Identify any hard time constraints such as a closing date, lease renewal, or urgent health concern driving the timeline.

questions.title: What is your budget for the inspection and any follow-up testing?
questions.description: Understand the financial limit to recommend the right tier of inspection service.

questions.title: What will you do with the inspection results once you have them?
questions.description: Clarify the end goal — peace of mind, a formal report for a third party, or a remediation plan — to define what a successful outcome looks like.

questions.title: Are there visible signs of mold or a specific area of concern?
questions.description: Find out if there is already visible mold, water damage, or a musty smell pointing to a specific problem area in the basement.
